name: Mohur
summary:
Mohur is a two-player card game of trading and set collection. The two players act as rival merchants dealing in a common market along the Company route, buying and selling diamonds, gold, silver, cloth, spice and leather for rupees. The title refers to the mohur, a gold coin of Mughal and later British India, represented in the game by coin cards. A match is played as a best of three rounds and typically lasts 10 to 15 minutes.

Each turn consists of exactly one action. A player may take a single good from the five-card market, exchange two or more market goods for an equal number of cards from hand or coin reserve, collect every coin in the market, or discard cards of one type to claim that good's tokens. Token values fall as each stack is depleted, rewarding early sales, and diamonds, gold and silver can only be sold in sets of two or more. Selling three or more cards at once adds a randomly drawn bonus token, kept face down until scoring. A round ends once three token stacks are empty or the draw deck is exhausted. The player with more coins gains 5 rupees, totals are compared, and the winner receives a Company Seal; the first to two seals wins.
